title: FOREST v2.0 Assessment
description: A draft framework transcribing the FOREST Framework for Values-Driven Scholarly Communication, version 2.0 (Lippincott & Skinner, Educopia Institute, Spring 2022): 96 indicators under 23 principles and six values — Financial and organizational resilience, Openness, Responsible governance, Equity, accessibility and anti-oppression, Sharing of knowledge, and Transparency — each scored on FOREST's own four-step progress bar (Not planning, Considering, In progress, Implemented). Designed to recognise growth and progress rather than to grade.
aboutHtml:
The FOREST Framework for Values-Driven Scholarly Communication (Framework 2.0, Spring 2022) was developed by Sarah Lippincott and Katherine Skinner at the Educopia Institute, with the Next Generation Library Publishing team, with support from Arcadia — a charitable fund of Lisbet Rausing and Peter Baldwin. Its six values — Financial and organizational resilience, Openness, Responsible governance, Equity, accessibility, and anti-oppression, Sharing of knowledge, and Transparency — come from dozens of manifestos and open letters by faculty, students, publishers, librarians, and open source tool developers. Each value has principles (23 in total), and each principle has indicators (a, b, c, …) that show how it can look in practice, with example evidence.

Here every indicator is one item to assess, grouped by value, with FOREST's codes (F1a, O3c, …) kept in the titles. The indicator wording follows the framework's overview sheets; the principle, whether an indicator applies to mature communities, whether it is aimed specifically at publishers or at software & infrastructure providers, and the evidence FOREST proposes (and whether it should be public or internal) are in each item's description. Of the 96 indicators, 39 apply to mature or well-established communities only (marked with an asterisk in FOREST); the rest apply to communities at all stages.

The scale is FOREST's own progress bar, modeled on the FAIR Data Maturity Model: Not planning (applicable, but no current plans), Considering (documentable actions to develop a roadmap), In progress (documentable actions to move towards adherence) and Implemented (fully adheres, with evidence). The framework's “Not applicable” is expressed by leaving an indicator unanswered. The level descriptions are FOREST's own, repeated for every indicator.

A caution from the authors: the progress bar “is not meant to be used as a grading or rating system, nor do we encourage communities to tally a final score or average”. This tool shows counts and a summary percentage for every framework; for FOREST, read them as a rough overview of where effort is concentrated, not as a score. The framework also comes with a reflective practice question set per principle, which is not reproduced here — see the source. FOREST does not claim extensibility beyond North America and parts of Europe.

Licensed CC BY 4.0. Suggested citation: Lippincott, S., & Skinner, K. (2022). FOREST Framework for Values-Driven Scholarly Communication. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6557302. This is a transcription of the PDF by this tool (with AI assistance) and is a draft pending review; it is not an official FOREST instrument.
